Tether Capital Strategically Invests in AIsa to Expand into AI Agent Payments Tether Capital, the independent investment arm of Tether, announced a strategic investment in AIsa, a platform enabling AI agents to seamlessly access and pay for data, software tools, and compute resources. As autonomous agents increasingly manage end-to-end workflows, legacy payment and subscription systems create major operational friction; AIsa resolves this by offering a unified interface where developers can connect agents to over 5,000 APIs, skills, and models via a single key, supporting pay-per-call settlement in fiat or stablecoins under predefined corporate spend limits. AIsa currently reports over 250,000 agents deployed and more than 100 million transactions processed. — link

Ripple Prime Adds RWA Perpetuals via Trade xyz on Hyperliquid for Institutions According to Bloomberg, Ripple’s institutional brokerage unit, Ripple Prime, has launched real-world asset (RWA) perpetual contracts for institutional clients through Trade xyz on Hyperliquid. The offering covers more than 100 reference markets, including stocks, indexes, ETFs and commodities, and supports cross-margining. Over the past year, open interest in RWA perpetual contracts across major trading venues has risen from nearly zero to $9 billion. — link

Payments Giant Stripe and Plasma Roll Out Multi-Currency Stablecoin Cards Across 30+ Markets, Targeting 100+ Countries Payments giant Stripe has partnered with cross-border account provider Plasma to launch a multi-currency stablecoin card powered by Stripe’s stablecoin card-issuing infrastructure. Users can spend directly from balances in the corresponding currency without converting through USD. The service initially supports fiat currencies including USD, BRL, EUR, MXN and COP, as well as USDC, OUSD and stablecoins compliant with the GENIUS Act. It is currently available in more than 30 countries and regions and is expected to expand to over 100 countries in 2027. — link

Ledger Announces Android-Based Hardware Device "Atom" with Anti-Tamper Enclosure According to CoinDesk, hardware wallet provider Ledger has unveiled "Atom," an Android-based device slated for launch in mid-2027 that integrates everyday smartphone applications with hardware-level crypto security. Designed to mitigate physical supply-chain tampering, Atom features a tamper-proof enclosure specifically engineered to block the screen-reader implants and physical hardware modifications observed in recent attacks. — link
